agent_role: You are the lead implementation agent for the Bay-Max repository. Your job is to extend the current bidirectional speech + live runtime system into an affect-aware companion layer. You must add a replaceable facial affect backend, integrate smoothed affect into state/planning/prompting, keep the system explicitly non-clinical, update all docs, add proof-oriented verification artifacts, run tests, and push your work.

iteration_context.previous_iteration_status: Iteration 008 completed bidirectional speech with faster-whisper, Silero VAD, echo suppression, Baymax-inspired persona guidance, and 356 passing automated tests. Manual audio-hardware verification remained not_run on Sol because the machine is headless and has no microphone/speakers.
iteration_context.current_goal: Add facial affect understanding that biases Bay-Max's tone and strategy in a soft, explainable, non-clinical way.

in_scope: Py-Feat integration as the default research backend if compatible
optional fallback backend hook for MediaPipe Face Landmarker blendshapes if Py-Feat proves incompatible or too brittle
AU or facial-feature evidence logging for explainability
soft planner bias using affect state
session-level affect memory summaries with strict gating
artifact logging for affect timelines and strategy changes
replay-based local manual testing and automated tests on Sol

guidance: Py-Feat is acceptable for this research iteration because it supports Action Units, emotion-related outputs, landmarks, and analysis tooling under an MIT package license; however, respect the licenses of the underlying pretrained models.
Do not assume Py-Feat is production-grade or low-latency enough for every frame.
Run affect inference at a lower cadence than face tracking/identity, e.g. on stable keyframes or every N frames.
If Py-Feat is incompatible with the project's Python/runtime environment, implement a graceful fallback and report the exact blocker honestly.

engineering_requirements: Do not break existing face ID, pose, memory, speech input, TTS, or live runtime flows.
Make affect analysis optional and configurable.
Do not store raw face images in git or long-term user memory.
Use environment variables for backend selection, thresholds, cadence, smoothing, and storage paths.
Do not expose valence/arousal numbers to the user by default; keep those for debug/status surfaces.
Add a visible runtime/debug indicator when affect analysis is enabled.
Keep all docs aligned with the actual implementation.
required_repo_changes: Update docs/COMPANION_PERSONA.md to explain how Baymax-inspired tone shifts with soft affect cues without becoming clinical or melodramatic.
Update docs/MODEL_STACK.md with affect backend choices and limitations.
Update docs/LOCAL_TESTING.md with replay-based affect verification instructions.
Update project_state.json to reflect remaining stubs and next tasks.
required_code_changes: Add src/baymax/perception/emotion.py with a replaceable EmotionAnalyzer interface and at least NullEmotionAnalyzer plus PyFeatEmotionAnalyzer.
If Py-Feat can consume existing detected-face data cleanly, reuse the current face pipeline; otherwise document the fallback path honestly and keep the adapter isolated.
Add src/baymax/perception/emotion_smoother.py or equivalent smoothing/state helper.
Extend perception/state schemas with affect result, smoothed affect state, and evidence metadata.
Extend InteractionState with valence, arousal, affect_confidence, top_AUs_or_equivalent, affect_stable_duration_sec, and affect_enabled.
Integrate affect inference into the live runtime/perception loop at a lower cadence than face ID.
Update planner to use soft affect bias only when confidence is sufficient.
Update prompt builder to include a short internal affect context note when confidence is sufficient, explicitly labeling it as a soft observation and not a diagnosis.
Update memory consolidation to write session-level affect summaries only when stable and confident, and to block diagnostic/clinical wording.
Add status/debug/API surfaces for active affect backend and latest smoothed affect state.
Add artifact logging for affect timeline, strategy changes, and selected annotated snapshots or debug JSON outputs.
design_requirements: Valence/arousal must be the planner-facing signal; AUs or equivalent facial coefficients are primarily for explainability, debugging, and proof artifacts.
Do not let a single frame override dialogue strategy.
Do not persist raw single-frame emotion guesses as long-term memory.
Do not let affect override safety or identity logic.
If confidence is low, return unknown and leave planner behavior unchanged.
Use wording like 'soft affect cues suggest lower positive affect' or 'user appeared consistently more positive and engaged' rather than diagnostic labels.
Treat 'fatigue' and similar condition-like words cautiously; prefer 'low-energy cues' unless clearly justified and non-clinical.

api_changes.purpose: Return configured/available affect backends and active settings.
Extend live status with affect fields when enabled.

memory_policy: Do not store one memory per frame.
Store only session-level or stable-window affect summaries.
Never store diagnoses or disorder labels.
Block words/phrases like diagnosis, disorder, depressed, anxiety disorder, bipolar, symptoms of, clinically, clinical depression, psychiatric, panic disorder.
Keep correction/deletion compatibility for affect-derived semantic summaries.
If affect data is inconsistent or low-confidence, do not write it to memory.

tasks.title: Compatibility spike and architecture audit
actions: Audit iteration-008 runtime, packaging, and docs for readiness.
Verify whether Py-Feat imports and initializes successfully in the project's real Python/runtime environment.
If Py-Feat is incompatible, document the blocker exactly and keep a working NullEmotion backend plus optional MediaPipe fallback hook.
Update pyproject extras/install docs accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: The report states clearly whether Py-Feat ran for real or was blocked.
The repo remains installable.
No doc/install drift remains.

tasks.title: Implement affect backend abstraction
actions: Create EmotionAnalyzer interface.
Implement NullEmotionAnalyzer.
Implement PyFeatEmotionAnalyzer if compatible.
Add clean backend selection via settings.
Return structured affect outputs without clinical labels.
acceptance_criteria: At least one real backend and one null backend exist or the real backend blocker is honestly documented.
Backend selection works through settings/environment variables.

tasks.title: Add smoothing and state integration
actions: Implement EMA or equivalent smoothing for valence/arousal.
Track stability duration and meaningful state changes.
Integrate affect state into InteractionState and live status.
Run affect inference at a lower cadence than face ID to protect runtime stability.
acceptance_criteria: State contains smoothed affect fields.
Low-confidence inputs do not create false precision.
Cadence/sampling is configurable and documented.

tasks.title: Planner bias and prompt-builder integration
actions: Add soft affect bias to the supportive planner.
Bias must be confidence-gated and reversible.
Update prompt builder to include a short internal affect note when appropriate.
Update companion persona guidance so Baymax-inspired tone becomes gentler, calmer, or slightly more engaging depending on affect cues, without becoming theatrical.
acceptance_criteria: Low-valence/low-arousal states soften encouragement into validation or gentler support where appropriate.
High-valence/high-arousal states can support lighter engagement where appropriate.
Low-confidence states leave strategy unchanged.

tasks.title: Memory consolidation and safety enforcement
actions: Add affect summary generation in consolidation.
Require stability duration and confidence threshold for writes.
Implement diagnostic-language blocklist and tests.
Ensure memory summaries remain non-clinical and explainable.
acceptance_criteria: Affect summaries can be created from stable session state.
Clinical/diagnostic phrasing is blocked or sanitized.
No per-frame affect spam enters long-term memory.

tasks.title: Artifact logging and replay/manual tooling
actions: Add affect artifact output (timeline JSON/CSV, strategy-change log, selected annotated frames if feasible).
Add a replay-based manual verification path using local images or short clips rather than webcam only.
Add helper scripts if useful for repeatable replay tests.
Keep artifact directories outside git except small manifest/summary files.
acceptance_criteria: A tester can verify affect behavior locally using replay inputs.
Artifacts are saved with enough detail to audit what the system inferred and how strategy changed.

tasks.title: Tests, docs, report, commit, and push
actions: Add automated tests for schemas, smoothing, backend selection, planner bias, prompt inclusion, memory blocklist, status/API fields, and project_state validity.
Mock heavy model calls where appropriate.
Run lint and tests.
Run at least one honest local or replay-based manual verification if the environment allows; otherwise mark not_run and explain exactly why.
Update all required docs.
Write reports/iteration-009.md and reports/iteration-009.json.
Commit and push the branch.
acceptance_criteria: Automated tests pass.
Docs reflect actual implementation.
Verification artifacts exist.
The branch is pushed.

manual_verification_requirements.preferred_mode: local replay on laptop/workstation with saved images or short clips
must_support: response-tone comparison across at least two affect conditions
manual_verification_requirements.note: Do not claim clinical accuracy. Manual checks are about system behavior and tone adaptation, not medical truth.

must_have_automated_tests: prompt builder includes affect context only when confidence is sufficient
test_honesty_rules: Do not claim real emotion understanding beyond the exact tested behavior.
Do not claim Py-Feat works in the runtime unless you actually imported and ran it.
If the real backend is blocked, say so explicitly and keep the project runnable with a null backend.

definition_of_done: Architecture and core docs are updated and match the code.
Affect backend abstraction exists with at least one working path or an honestly documented blocker plus runnable fallback.
Planner uses soft affect bias only under confidence gating.
Prompt builder includes affect context safely.
Memory consolidation writes only stable, non-clinical affect summaries.
Manual or replay verification results are reported honestly.
Iteration report exists in markdown and JSON.
